_readme: Acquisition registry for Darśana texts. Every entry was CHECKED, not assumed — several
sources that looked promising turned out to be unusable, and those are kept here with the
ready   — machine-readable Unicode/IAST text, scriptable, licence workable
ocr     — real content but scanned images; needs a Devanagari OCR pass
images  — manuscript facsimiles; feeds the HTR/OCR queue, not the text index
blocked — robots-disallowed, licence-incompatible, or technically inaccessible
Licensing follows dge/PROJECT_STATUS.md convention #5: absence of a licence is not
permission, and each unlicensed source needs a specific logged decision from the project

sources.name: GRETIL — Göttingen Register of Electronic Texts in Indian Languages
sources.format: UTF-8 romanised IAST (NOT Devanagari) — transliteration is a pipeline step
sources.why_first: the only source with substantial machine-readable Nyāya AND Mīmāṃsā text, and this repo already has importers/gretil.py to extend
notes: Two generations coexist: legacy .../1_sanskr/6_sastra/3_phil/{nyaya,vaisesika,mimamsa}/<code>_u.htm with a parallel <code>_r.txt raw text; and the newer TEI corpus at /gretil/corpustei/sa_<title>.xml.
Prefer the _r.txt / TEI .xml variants — cleaner than the _u.htm.
Directory listings return HTTP 403; you must parse gretil.html for hrefs.
Every file carries: 'THIS GRETIL TEXT FILE IS FOR REFERENCE PURPOSES ONLY! COPYRIGHT AND TERMS OF USAGE AS FOR SOURCE FILE.' Parse and RETAIN the per-file source attribution block.
sources.licence: per-file; GRETIL defers to each e-text's original contributor (SANSKNET, Muktabodha, etc.)
sources.scraper_sketch: GET gretil.html once; regex hrefs matching 3_phil/(nyaya|vaisesika|mimamsa)/ and corpustei/.*\.xml. Prefer _r.txt / TEI. Strip the header block up to the TEXT marker, capture the source-attribution lines into a provenance field, transliterate IAST→Devanagari. Never request directory listings (403).

sources.name: SanskritDocuments.org
sources.format: ITRANS .itx source + generated Unicode Devanagari HTML + PDF
notes: Own Nyāya/Mīmāṃsā corpus is thin: Tarkasaṅgraha (with Dīpikā) and a second Tarkasaṅgraha recension. Most value is the links-out page.
https://sanskritdocuments.org/sanskrit/nyaya/ does NOT exist (404) — there is no dedicated Nyāya category.
sources.licence: RESTRICTIVE. Attribution and a backlink to the original are mandatory; must not be used to drive traffic or ad revenue; 'meant to be used for personal study and research'. See https://sanskritdocuments.org/copyingproblem.html — email them before any bulk mirroring.
sources.scraper_sketch: GET the category indexes (doc_z_misc_major_works/, TextsElsewhere/), follow .itx links rather than HTML (richest markup), parse the .itx header (\itxtitle, encoding, proofreader credits) into provenance, convert ITRANS→Devanagari, emit a visible backlink.

sources.name: OPenn — University of Pennsylvania Kislak Center
sources.format: manuscript facsimile images + TEI metadata (NO transcription)
sources.licence: BEST OF ANY SOURCE HERE. Images: Public Domain Mark 1.0 ('free of known copyright restrictions and in the public domain'). Metadata: CC-BY-4.0.
notes: https://openn.library.upenn.edu/Data/0002/ is an OPEN APACHE DIRECTORY INDEX — fully enumerable.
Ms. Coll. 390 is the Schoenberg Indic collection; item 632 is the Sāmānyanirukti of Gadādharabhaṭṭācārya, 19c, 32 folios.
sources.scraper_sketch: Walk the Apache index at /Data/0002/, fetch each <item>/data/<item>_TEI.xml, filter on textLang and subject for Sanskrit + Nyāya/Mīmāṃsā, then pull data/web/*.jpg listed in <facsimile>.

sources.name: Karnataka Sanskrit University — Sambhāṣā Tarkasaṅgraha collection
sources.format: scanned PDFs of printed editions, 1849–1963 prints plus modern reprints
sources.scale: 45 PDFs, each a full printed book (100–600 pp)
sources.why_valuable: the densest Tarkasaṅgraha commentary corpus found anywhere — Dīpikā in many editions, Nyāyabodhinī, Padakṛtya, Nīlakaṇṭhī, Bhāskarodaya, Dīpikāprakāśa, Sarvasva, Phakkikā, Kamalā/Indumatī, Nyāyaśekhara, Sukhapraveśinī, Lakṣaṇaṭippaṇī, plus Ballantyne/Hultzsch/Kuppuswami translations
notes: The listing page and the PDF directory have DIFFERENT names (tarkasangraha/ vs Tarka%20Sangraha/); filenames are full bibliographic strings containing spaces and commas.
Plain static HTML, GET only. No stated licence anywhere on the page.
sources.licence_risk: pre-1930 prints (Ballantyne 1849/1851, Vidyasagar 1872, BSS 1918, Venkateswara Press) are safely public domain; MLBD/Chowkhamba reprints are likely in copyright — filter by edition date before ingesting
sources.next_step: enumerate the 45 PDF URLs from the one static index page, download the pre-1930 subset, run Devanagari OCR (expect poor quality on pothi-format and 19c items)

sources.name: Central Sanskrit University e-books (sanskrit.nic.in)
sources.blocker: the host presents an INCOMPLETE TLS CERTIFICATE CHAIN — every fetch failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. Fixable client-side by supplying the correct intermediate/CA bundle.
sources.promise: these are freshly typeset Devanagari PDFs produced under a content-generation project, so they very likely carry an extractable text layer — test pdftotext on one before committing effort. If they do, this moves to tier 'ready'.
titles_confirmed: Dictionary of Nyāya Terms (V. N. Jha, 2 parts)

sources.name: Internet Archive / Digital Library of India
sources.why: the actual home of Pañcalakṣaṇī-class scans now that epustakalay is gone; ~422k DLI PDFs, and a real public API
sources.note: use the archive.org metadata API for enumeration; per-item rights vary — check each

sources.name: TarkaSangraha.com
sources.verdict: NOT USABLE — this was expected to be the flagship source and is not one
findings: Client-rendered app; every content page returns only a shell. No Sanskrit body text in the served HTML.
The site says of itself: 'Website is under initial stages of development.' Placeholder copy reads 'Here, we will have a word cloud of the topics in several books.'
The promised per-section reader does not exist — there are no per-chapter URLs. Sitemap lists 17 pages total, mostly essays.
Sitemap declares host www.tarkasangraha.com, which does not resolve in DNS; only the apex works.
Footer: '© 2026 Tarka Sangraha. All rights reserved.' No open licence.
sources.revisit: worth an email to the maintainer, and worth re-checking in 6–12 months

sources.name: e-BharatiSampat
sources.verdict: robots.txt disallows crawling — every fetch including /robots.txt itself returns ROBOTS_DISALLOWED
sources.id_scheme_decoded: the id/bookid params are plain base64 of a zero-padded numeric string — e.g. MDc4MzkyMDU2NDQxMjkz decodes to 078392056441293. Endpoints: /readSearch.php?id=<b64>, /readbook3.php?bookid=<b64>&pageno=<b64>, raw PDFs at /pdfs/<unix_timestamp>.pdf
sources.note: IDs are non-sequential, so enumeration is impossible even if crawling were permitted
sources.next_step: request permission from the operators (IGNCA / Bharatiya Sampada project) rather than scraping

sources.name: Bharatavani
sources.verdict: LICENCE-INCOMPATIBLE, and it has no Nyāya content anyway
sources.licence_quote: content must be distributed 'in its "as is" form' — 'No person is permitted to adapt, translate, alter, summarize, or make any derivation'
sources.note: that clause forbids the segmentation and normalisation any text pipeline performs. The Sanskrit section is popular/literary (Cāṇakyanīti, Uttararāmacaritam, Gītā ṭīkā) — no Pañcalakṣaṇī, no Nyāya śāstra corpus.

sources.name: ePustakalay
sources.verdict: DOMAIN HIJACKED — now serves Indonesian slot-gambling spam. No ebook content remains. DO NOT INGEST.
